content: This medication may increase your sensitivity to sunlight. It is advised to limit your exposure to the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen while wearing protective clothing when outdoors. Children under the age of 8 may be more susceptible to side effects of tigecycline, particularly tooth discoloration. Tooth discoloration has also been observed in older children and young adults. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. You should not become pregnant while using tigecycline, as it may harm an unborn baby. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function, fibrinogen levels, blood counts, and cultures, may be conducted while you are using this medication. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, it is important to take the medication as scheduled. For storage instructions, consult the product guidelines and your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Side effects such as nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, or pain/swelling at the injection site may occur. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. Rarely, tetracycline drugs like tigecycline may cause increased pressure around the brain (intracranial hypertension). This risk is higher in overweight women of childbearing age or those with a history of intracranial hypertension. If this condition develops, it usually resolves after stopping tigecycline, but there is a potential for permanent vision loss or blindness. This medication may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using tigecycline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to tetracyclines (such as doxycycline, minocycline, tetracycline), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Tigecycline may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (such as the typhoid vaccine).
